text:
carla: Hey team — invoice from DeepEyes Pvt Ltd (IN) landed but vendor didn't attach tax doc. They're asking for full payment, says their bank needs cleared funds.

carla: Invoice snippet:
```
INV-2026-2109
Vendor: DeepEyes Pvt Ltd, GSTIN: 27ABCDE1234F1Z5
Billed to: Redwood Inc (US)
Amount: $18,000
Tax: -- (vendor states non-US services)
Payment terms: 30 days
```

rajiv-vendor: Hi Carla — Rajiv here from DeepEyes. We're an Indian company providing ML inference tuning. We sent invoice to Redwood US entity. We don't have a US TIN. Please confirm whether you need W-8BEN-E or if Redwood can gross-up so we receive net amount after US withholding.

sarah: Tax: If payment is made by the US entity to a foreign vendor, the payer must determine U.S. tax withholding unless vendor provides a valid W-8. Without a completed W-8BEN-E we would withhold 30% on reportable US-source services.

mike: Sales: We believed this was billed to Redwood India or Redwood UK. @lina-sales can you confirm which legal entity the PO referenced? If it's the US entity we need W-8, otherwise different rules apply.

lina-sales: PO references Redwood US (Redwood, Inc) and purchase order PO-6743. Client asked to bill Redwood US for contractual reasons. We're chasing vendor for W-8 but they asked about gross-up because invoiced amount is what they expect to receive.

invoicebot: Invoice INV-2026-2109 uploaded to NetSuite. Hold code: TAX_DOC_MISSING. Payment blocked.

sarah: Options: (1) Ask vendor to complete and return a signed W-8BEN-E (preferred) — no withholding if a treaty or if services are foreign-source (we'll validate). (2) If vendor refuses, we must withhold 30% on US-source services and remit to IRS; we can provide an amount payable after withholding but we generally do not gross-up. (3) If sales can reissue PO to a non-US Redwood entity, finance can pay without W-8.

carla: Rajiv — can you complete W-8BEN-E and send signed PDF? If you can't, do you accept payment after 30% withholding? We typically don't do gross-ups for one-off vendors.

rajiv-vendor: We'll try to complete W-8BEN-E but need help. Also ask: our services were delivered remotely from India; isn't that foreign-source and not subject to US withholding?

sarah: Good question. For U.S. withholding, the source of services is determined by where services are performed. If all work was performed outside the U.S., it may be foreign-source and not subject to US withholding — but we need documentation (statement from vendor) and to confirm the paying entity. W-8BEN-E still helpful to certify foreign status.

mike: Lina — can you check the PO and onboarding notes for location of work and whether Sales can switch billing to Redwood EMEA or Redwood APAC? That might avoid US withholding.

lina-sales: I'll follow up with account and vendor. Quick note: vendor asked for payment timeline if W-8 sent today.

carla: Finance: once W-8 received, we'll validate, update NetSuite, and release payment. If vendor declines and we still pay US entity, we'll calculate withholding and send payment advice showing gross vs withholding.

rajiv-vendor: Thanks — we'll return completed W-8BEN-E tonight and a brief statement confirming work done in India.

sarah: Perfect — please include the vendor's registered address, confirmation of country where services were performed, and sign/date. That should let us proceed without withholding if validated.

carla: Thanks all — holding until W-8 received.
